lessons.title: Greetings
lessons.content:
Hola means hello. Use Buenos días in the morning, Buenas tardes in the afternoon and Buenas noches in the evening or at night.

To say goodbye use Adiós or Hasta luego. To ask how someone is, say ¿Cómo estás?

lessons.title: Introducing yourself
lessons.content: Me llamo Ana means 'My name is Ana'. Soy de Filipinas means 'I am from the Philippines'. When you meet someone, say Mucho gusto: nice to meet you.

questions.text: How do you say 'My name is Ana'?

lessons.title: Numbers 1 to 10
lessons.content:
uno, dos, tres, cuatro, cinco, seis, siete, ocho, nueve, diez.

Practice by counting things around you out loud.

lessons.title: Ordering food
lessons.content: Quisiera... means 'I would like...'. Ask for the check with La cuenta, por favor. Ask a price with ¿Cuánto cuesta? Agua means water.

questions.text: How do you politely ask for the check?

skills.title: Intro to Python
skills.description: Write your first programs in Python.

lessons.title: Variables and print
lessons.content:
A variable stores a value: name = 'Ana'. You do not declare a type in Python.

print(name) shows the value on the screen.

lessons.title: Numbers and strings
lessons.content:
Whole numbers are int (7), decimals are float (3.14) and text is str ('hello').

+ adds numbers (2 + 3 is 5) but joins strings ('2' + '3' is '23').

questions.text: Which of these is a float?

How does Python group the lines under an if?

lessons.title: Loops
lessons.content:
for i in range(3): runs three times with i = 0, 1, 2.

while keeps repeating as long as its condition is true.

questions.text: How many times does 'for i in range(3)' run?
Which loop repeats while a condition is true?

skills.title: Photoshop Basics
skills.description: Layers, selections and your first edits.

lessons.title: Interface and layers
lessons.content:
The Layers panel stacks your content: the top layer covers the ones below it. The eye icon shows or hides a layer.

Keep things on separate layers so you can change one part without touching the rest.

questions.text: What does the eye icon on a layer do?

options: To edit one part without affecting the rest

lessons.title: Selection tools
lessons.content: Marquee draws rectangles and ellipses. Lasso draws a freehand outline. Magic Wand selects areas of similar colour with one click.

questions.text: Which tool selects similar colours with one click?
Which tool draws a freehand selection?

lessons.title: Widgets and the widget tree
lessons.content:
In Flutter everything on screen is a widget, and widgets nest inside each other to form a tree.

Scaffold gives a screen its basic structure. Column stacks children vertically and Row places them side by side.

questions.text: Which widget lays children out vertically?

lessons.title: Stateless vs Stateful
lessons.content: A StatelessWidget never changes after it is built. A StatefulWidget has a State object, and calling setState tells Flutter to rebuild with the new values.

skills.title: Guitar Basics
skills.description: Tune up and play your first chords.

lessons.title: Parts and tuning
lessons.content:
Main parts: headstock (with the tuning pegs), neck, body and bridge.

Standard tuning, from the thickest string to the thinnest, is E A D G B E.

questions.text: Standard tuning, thickest to thinnest string?
options: E A D G B E
A B C D E F
G D A E B G
E E E E E E

lessons.title: Your first chords
lessons.content:
Em (E minor) and Am (A minor) are two of the easiest open chords. Press the strings just behind the fret, not on top of it.

For Em you strum all six strings. For Am you skip the thickest string.

questions.text: Which string do you usually skip when strumming Am?

skills.title: UI/UX Design Basics
skills.description: Design screens people can actually use.

lessons.title: What is UX?
lessons.content: UI is how a product looks: colours, buttons, type. UX is how it feels to use. Good UX is clear, efficient and accessible, so people reach their goal without thinking about the interface.

lessons.title: Wireframes
lessons.content: A wireframe is a simple sketch of a screen's layout. It shows structure, not colours or final images. Make them before the visual design because they are quick and cheap to change.
